task:
Well, <Ranger>. You wanna collaborate in exchange for a favor? Okay, I have one little job for you.
As I hope you know, the world of politics is a mob of brutal predators. Each of them tries to eat up the competition to get ahead. I'm one of those predators. And I want to, figuratively speaking, eat up one of my opponents. There will be an election in our star system soon, and he's put together a fantastic PR campaign. What's more, he's purchased several corporations, which is sure to give him a lot of clout at the voting booth. But I'm not planning on losing the position I've had for so long, so I need to smear this guy so hard he'll never wash clean again.
You, <Ranger>, need to plant some dirt in this guy's apartment so it'll be found later during a random search. That'll destroy him as a politician. I've consulted with my aides, and we decided that it should be an illegal drug. On our planet we've got a huge problem with juveniles getting hooked on this...stuff. The public will crucify him if it's found in his apartment.
Right now this politician is living on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system, where he's running his election campaign. If you agree to help me for the sake of our future partnership, then when you arrive my assistant will meet you, give you everything you need, and tell you how to break into the residence. Are you ready to handle such a delicate mission?
success:
Excellent, <Ranger>! You couldn't have done better work! I laughed 'till I cried when his dumbfounded face appeared on the evening news. I even recorded that part, so I can watch it again from time to time to renew my motivation and make me feel better about myself.
As far as our arrangement goes, I think you've completed your part of the bargain, and now you can count on my support. Thanks again. And don't forget that if you tell anybody about the incident, I will be very, very disappointed in you.
loc.1.0:
You landed at the spaceport of the planet's moon, in the very center of an enormous gigopolis made of plastic and concrete. Gigantic skyscrapers rise above your head with streams of dense air traffic bustling between them. Your "mark", the person whose life you are to ruin, probably lives in one of these huge buildings. 
For a moment you thought about what would have happened if you had met your victim first and he had given you a mission to smear your current employer. It probably would have changed the world. However, even the flapping of butterfly wings changes the world, so you decided not to stress about it, tossing philosophy aside and heading toward the taxi stop.
loc.2.0:
You got out of the taxi when it brought you to the address which your employer had given you. An intermediary should meet you here somewhere.
"Are you <Ranger>?" a voice asked behind your back.
You whipped around and saw a lean, middle-aged fae. His face was hidden by a wide-brimmed hat. He held a rolled-up newspaper in his hands.
"Follow me," he said after you responded positively to his question.
You entered a small cafe on the corner of the building and sat at the table farthest from the door.
"He lives in this building on the fortieth floor. There's only one apartment on the entire floor, so you can't miss it," said the fae when the waiter left. He didn't beat around the bush. "Here's a copy of the key to the entrance. There's also a backup lock installed that takes a code. The code is a four digit number. I confess that we have a problem. We have three codes, but we don't know which one is right. Memorize all three just in case. Here they are: [p30], [p31] and [p32]. The first is the year he was born, and he probably didn't have enough imagination for the other two. Is everything clear so far?"
You nodded your head.
"His apartment is relatively small. A hallway, two rooms, a kitchen, and a bathroom. Don't get lost. Be extremely cautious inside. If you touch anything, be sure to put it back where it was. He mustn't suspect anything, otherwise he will call in witnesses and the police, and our plan will be spoiled. And don't be overly zealous when you're hiding the evidence - if you do it too well, the cops may never find it. Here, take this."
He pushed the rolled-up newspaper over to your side of the table.
"Watch it - don't unroll the paper here. It has five packages with the drug inside. Hide them all in different places. That bundle also includes sterile gloves and shoe booties," he said. "According to our information, you have [p1] minutes before the politician completes his business and returns home, so try to stay within that deadline. We meet again here later to discuss how it went.
loc.2.1:
The fae silently raised his hand and his sleeve dropped to reveal an intricate electronic bracelet.
"If I get within a hundred meters of him or his apartment, an alarm will go off and within a minute I'd be cuffed in the back seat of a police car. Now if I've answered your questions, get to your business."
loc.3.0:
You took the elevator up to the required floor and, trying to look natural, peered out. Directly in front of you was a small hallway with an impressive door on the opposite end. 
Sneaking closer, you stared at it doubtfully. The massive hinges and metal plates looked very solid. If you didn't have a key, you would have had to saw at the hinges for hours - and the noise that cause...
The keyhole could be seen on the door on the side opposite from the hinges and, a bit higher, the combination lock's control unit. The combination lock's screen was disabled. You don't have much time, so you'd better start breaking in.

loc.12.0:
"Problems?" asked the fae, looking at you. "I didn't say anything about problems. I'm surprised how clean you were. Most of the things were in their places, according to the report. And no fingerprints at all. It seems you're not so hopeless after all." 
You exhaled a deep sigh of relief.
loc.13.0:
Of course, you didn't forget to remove the gloves and stuff them in the pocket of your ranger uniform and take the booties off of your shoes, although you only did this after a while when you garnered several suspicious looks when descending in the elevator.

Now you have to wait a couple of hours until the forces of law and order strike the apartment and discover your illegal handiwork.

You strolled to the nearest park where you passed the time pleasantly, watching the pigeons and girls until it came time to return. You went to the cafe where your meeting was held before the operation. The fae was already inside, but you still went straight to the counter and ordered a small cup of coffee and a salad. They told you your order would be ready in a minute.

The fae nodded when you came to his table. You couldn't read anything from his face.
"Sit," he said, motioning toward a chair.
You obediently sat down and fixed your eyes on him, but the fae had barely opened his mouth to say something when a waiter appeared with plates. The fae scowled.

A special feature of the landscape in this residence is the Jacuzzi. The far side is barely visible with the naked eye, and a sign by the steps warns "No swimming beyond the buoys." Only the shelf with various cosmetics installed above the sink could compete with the Jacuzzi in its epicness.
Besides these, there is a toilet in the nearest corner, and a washing machine next to that, and next to that - a waste basket delicately covered with a lid.
A small ventilation hole with a grate is located behind the toilet.

loc.42.0:

Your sharp ranger sense for trouble eventually kicked in and rudely yanked you by the collar out of a dream, but you had still wasted several precious minutes.
loc.43.0:
You drummed your fingers for a while on the glass to get the fishes' attention. It would have been better if you hadn't. In response to your knocking, from somewhere in the dark depths of the aquarium flew an enormous predatory fish. If not for the glass, which crunched plaintively when struck by the bloodthirsty monster, you would have been swallowed whole. You entire life - short but full - had flashed before your eyes.
As you recovered from the memories of your school years, the fish again gained speed and created such a wave in the aquarium that the chaotic water splashed through a ventilation hole in the tank lid and drenched you from head to toe.

You quickly jumped back from the aquarium to stop irritating the monster. Small cracks had already appeared in the glass.

loc.82.0: The refrigerator is entirely empty, to your great chagrin. But maybe this is for the best, otherwise you would have lost control and scarfed something down.
loc.83.0: This is the latest model of one of those miraculous food processors that can do everything. They can almost compose music and fight dominators. Its surface is covered with mysterious winking lights, and numerous holes and chutes begging for something to be stuffed inside. The important thing is to not put your fingers in.
loc.85.0: You dug a small hole, like a penchekryak preparing to relieve himself, then placed a package with evidence in the depression, delicately sprinkled it with soil, and patted it down with your palm to hide your tracks.
loc.86.0: Even though drying floors is not a ranger job, you can't stand the sight of such a mess, so you rolled up your sleeves and worked as a housemaid for a couple minutes.

Sibolusofts are very gentle and frail animals, so they must be treated with love and kindness. They are also easily frightened and can actually die from even the slightest emotional trama.
If a sibolusoft gets upset, you have to play or sing something melodious to calm it down. Sibolusofts become very attached to their owners. If its owner dies, a sibolusoft can also die from depression," you read in the first book you came across. 

The title, "Breeding Sibolusofts", was printed conspicuously on the cover of this book authored by Niklaai Doozdov.
loc.89.0: You grabbed a bottle, whichever one your hand fell on, and, in order to avoid smudging any glasses, you poured its contents liberally into your mouth and, partly onto your jacket.
loc.89.1: The next bottle was as cold as ice, but that didn't scare you off - and you enthusiastically hit the bottle. In principle, this wouldn't have been half bad, expect your lips froze to the bottle.
loc.89.2: The drink was so stung so badly that you quickly grabbed another bottle to extinguish the fire in your nasal passages. This seemed to help, since afterward you stopped having any sensation at all.

"A quest must have a beginning and an end. The quest begins when, upon the ranger landing on a planet, the player clicks 'Accomplish quest'. Upon completing the quest the ranger remains on the same planet. During the fulfillment of a quest, the ranger may succeed or fail in his mission, die, and earn money or lose it. After successful completion of a quest, the attitude of the planet's government toward the ranger may improve (if, for example, he saved population from cholera), worsen (if the ranger performed illegal actions), or remain unchanged. After completion of a quest, no additional changes can be made to the ranger."

The cover modestly invited you to "ReadMe". The author's last name wasn't shown.
loc.91.0:
"He opened to the middle of the first book he came across and found a description of some sort of animal with an unpronounceable name starting with 'S'. He wasn't interested in it at all and set the book aside. In the next book he encountered some technical mumbo-jumbo that instantly made him grind his teeth. Hoping to find something worthwhile at least one, he picked out yet another book and opened it. It was a fictional story about a ranger who studied bookshelves in somebody else's apartment. In the first book he came across there was a description of some sort of animal with an unpronounceable..."

You quickly slammed the book closed and didn't even look to see who the author was.
loc.93.0: You smelled a small flower. Beautiful!
loc.93.3: Some pollen must have gotten up your nose, because you sneezed so powerfully that you spit all over the flowers. "Well, to hell with that plant!," you decided.
loc.96.0:
You quickly undressed and plopped into the warm water. After dipping under a couple of times to warm up, you swam with a noisy butterfly stroke toward the sunset. After a couple of minutes the buoys were behind you. Like a true ranger, you didn't pay any attention to them. Consequently, you swam into a warm current. All of your surroundings were shrouded in fog. You began to feel fatigued, but you couldn't tell which way to swim.
Finally, battered and worn, you threw yourself onto some shore. Feeling rough sand under your cheek, you glanced up and saw an enormous palm tree growing right on the water.
After half an hour you had recovered enough to crawl all the way onto the shore. Wild jungle encroached on the water from all sides. A suspicion crept into your head that this wasn't a Jacuzzi after all and that you had been washed away somewhere. But you hadn't finished pondering this shocking revelation when somebody coughed gently behind you. For moral and ethical reasons, you covered up as much of yourself as possible with your hands and then turned around.
"Hey, hot stuff!" said a voluptuous, tropical babe wearing a minimal amount of clothing.
"Uh..." you responded readily.
"I want you right now!" cried the girl and...

Whoa! What a dream! Not only were you torn away at the most interesting part, you also wasted precious time!
loc.98.0: You grabbed hold of the grate and yanked hard. The builder must not have expected somebody to entertain himself this way, since he didn't make the grate vandal-resistant. It tore right off, together with a piece of the wall, and you went flying back and crashed onto your rear end. Once the grate was entirely ripped off, hiding the evidence in the ventilation hole somehow didn't seem so relevant anymore.
loc.99.0: You carefully unscrewed the bolts from the grate and removed it without making a sound or any mess. Then you placed a package with evidence inside and tightened the screws back on the grate. Now the important thing is to remember to return the screwdriver to its place.
loc.100.0: You got unbuttoned, took care of your ranger needs, buttoned yourself back up, and pressed the flusher button, feeling that you had done your duty.
loc.101.0:
You sat down on the toilet, opened to the middle of the magazine, and began to read an article about some multimillionaire who loved gorgeous heifers and hot wheels, and had them by the dozens. Of course, what you didn't understand was why the pictures in the article showed expensive cars and scantily clad women. After all, the article hadn't said a word about them.

What rubbish! This magazine doesn't even come close to the latest issue of "Ranger Pride".
loc.102.0: With great effort, you moved the tank lid to the side and tossed in a package. Then you put the lid back in place. Now you can only hope that nobody flushes the toilet before the police search the tank.
loc.103.0: You pulled the magazine out from under the pillow and opened it. Inside were mostly pictures of half-dressed girls at exotic resort locations or on luxurious yachts.
loc.105.0: You crammed a package into one of the openings. To your horror, the processor took this as a call to action and started running. No one knows what processes were taking place inside, but in three minutes it grunted and spit a green cube onto a saucer. You decided not to risk tasting it. Would the police have enough courage to?
loc.106.0: You pushed the first button you came across and waited to see what would happen next. For a long time the processor puffed, grunted, and shuddered all over. Finally, it quieted down and released the product of its work on a small plate. You were slightly disappointed at the celebration of technological progress. Of course, You probably should have put something inside the food processor first.
loc.107.0:
You put the magazine inside and pressed a different button. The processor again began to purr and hum. After five minutes it released what it had produced. 
Of course. Spaghetti. How boring. Annoyed, you poked the slightly smoking pile of shredded paper on the plate. You wish you hadn't ruined that magazine. Though with some ketchup and vegetables...
loc.108.0:
"The problem, <Player>, is that even a penchekryak in the museum of fine art wouldn't have left more tracks that you managed too!"
Clearly irritated, the fae lifted a paper covered with text in a fine, bureaucratic-looking font.
"The police found no less than five pieces of irrefutable evidence of a break-in at the apartment," he said, throwing the paper aside in exasperation. "Naturally, the police can't shut their eyes to that many mistakes, so, congratulations, you successfully botched your mission. Get to the spaceport and fly away as soon as possible, before you're discovered."
The fae got up from the table and left without saying goodbye. It seems it would be best to follow his advice.
loc.109.0:
"The problem, <Ranger>, is that you didn't do your job well enough. The police discovered some evidence of a break-in at the residence. This isn't fatal - I know some people who can massage the search report, but they won't do it for the fun of it. I think you understand what I'm getting at."
"Hmm..." you replied, totally confused.
"Money, ranger. Money. It's all very simple. Give me <clr>5000<clrEnd> credits and you can walk. Otherwise, my police friends will be really upset and they'll start working hard for their legal income so their kids won't go hungry.
loc.111.0:
Blah, blah, blah, ranger!
(this version of the description shouldn't end up in the quest xD)
loc.111.1:
Judging by his appearance, the fae was beside himself with rage.
"I always knew that rangers were stupid, but I never suspected it could be this bad! I thought I gave you utterly precise instructions, the most important of which was 'Don't leave tracks.' But no. You're so recklessly indifferent to this important mission that you forgot the key to the front door! The cops aren't idiots, you know. As soon as they saw the scene they immediately realized that it was a dirty job. Now everybody knows that you did it. Good luck getting yourself out of this. I don't know you."

The fae stood and left without saying another word. As he walked out, the police walked in and, upon seeing you, immediately grabbed their guns from their holsters and shouted: 
"Stay where you are! You're under arrest!"

You put out your hand and tried to carefully adjust the painting, but you couldn't. You tugged on it, but the stubborn masterpiece wouldn't budge. You yanked it again without holding anything back and tore the colorful, incomprehensible-to-you piece of art off the wall.
On the wall behind the painting there is a combination lock, just like on the front door.
loc.114.0: A bit above the combination lock you noticed the hardware for hanging the painting. Getting the painting back in place only took a second, but it refused to hang evenly, constantly leaning to one side or the other. In the end you spit on the painting - figuratively, of course - and left it hanging the same way you found it.
loc.120.0: As soon as you pressed the last button, a previously inconspicuous wall panel, which was actually a secret door, flipped open in your face. Thanks to your sharp ranger reflexes you were able to avoid being hit in the nose - but just barely.
loc.121.0:
Your are in a spacious, and entirely pink, room. Directly in the middle of the room, under a pretentious pink chandelier is a huge doll house, also pink. The rest of the room is strewn with plush toys, dolls, and other signs of a happy childhood, which you, with your one and only cast-iron toy solider that was welded to the floor, will never understand. You eyes began to hurt from all the various spinning tops, tea sets, glitter, and tinsel. 
Well, even manly politicians who control the fate of millions of planet residents need to have their little weaknesses. It's good that this secret room is full of dolls and tinsel rather than chains and whips.
loc.122.0: You chose the largest mound of toys, dug down to its foundation, and then stuffed one of the packages with evidence in the crater you created. Putting the toys back was more of a challenge. You carefully placed a toy penchekryak (again pink) with plush teeth on the top of the pile and stepped back with the feeling of satisfaction that comes from a job well done.
loc.123.0: You sat on the floor, pulled a toy train closer, put dolls in each of the railcars, and rolled them around the room. The only thing you lacked to be completely happy was a train engineer's cap. You were having so much fun that you lost track of the time, so much so that if not for a random railroad emergency, which caused the train to crash into the wall, you would have kept playing all night.
loc.124.0:
The look of the room made you so happy that you decided to play a prank of this poor guy who loves pink so much. To implement your idea you needed the marker that was lying on the floor and the wall that was standing in its place. 
Sticking out your tongue from trying so hard, you began to draw crooked letters on the wall to form the phrase "Now I now", followed by an ellipsis with at least seven dots. You decided that this would really disturb the apartment's owner. After looking over your destructive work for a minute, you scribbled the letter 'k' at the beginning of the last word.
This will surely give the politician a few sleepless nights.
loc.125.0:
"Amazingly, <Ranger>, you did very well! The police didn't suspect a thing when they found the evidence you had planted. I guess you have a well-developed criminal mind. Or perhaps a detective's mind. Doesn't matter. In any event, you did a great job. Your promised reward is waiting for you on planet <FromPlanet>."
The fae got up from his seat and unexpectedly thrust his hand forward in the typical human gesture. You shook his purple and somewhat damp fingers. Then he turned and left without saying another word. Apparently, he was truly affected by your professionalism.
You breathed lightly and almost wanted to order a bottle of champagne, but then immediately pulled yourself together. The sooner you leave this planet the better - before any extraordinary circumstances come up.

You immediately exited the cafe, caught a taxi, said, "take me to the spaceport whippity-quick." Only when you got to your ship did you remember that you forgot to pay for your food. Well, you can't go back now. And what's more, somewhere in the distance you hear police sirens wailing. 
Quickly leaping into the cabin, you started the engine and darted away from the planet.
loc.126.0:
"So you're reasonable after all, <Ranger>," observed the fae. "I also would have paid. Although, for starters, I wouldn't have left so many tracks.
The fae folded the bills you had offered him and tucked them into an inner pocket.
loc.127.0:
Well, take care then, <Ranger>."
The fae finished his drink, grinned, and left the cafe. Just minutes later, police officers burst through the same door and immediately arrested you.

"<Ranger>, you did a horrible job with that evidence. Tell me, did you actually plant any in the apartment? Or did you just swing by for a tour and keep the narcotics for yourself? The police couldn't find anything useful. This creates certain problems for our informer, who told police about compromising evidence in the apartment. 
"They just don't know how to search! you responded, boiling with indignation.
"Really? Then you should have left them a list with a map of where to find your brilliant hiding places," laughed the fae. "I think you must already realize that you utterly failed your mission. Get to the spaceport and fly away as soon as possible, before you're discovered."
The fae got up from the table and left without saying goodbye. It seems it would be best to follow his advice.
loc.129.0:
"<Ranger>, you did a horrible job with that evidence. Instead of at least trying to hide it in some way, within reason, you scattered it about in plain view. I'm afraid you've completely botched your mission. Get to the spaceport and fly away as soon as possible, before you're discovered."

You worked diligently and blasted out an enormous pit. Then you almost got tangled up in the roots of the plant growing at your excavation site. The only problem was that you got quite a bit of dirt all over the previously clean floor.

Trying not to break the expensive device, you carefully pushed it a little to gain access to the rear panel. Then unfastened the latches holding the panel and moved it aside. It should have been a piece of cake to place a package inside, but you had barely stuck your hand in when there was a deafening crack and you were thrown back into the middle of the room. While you lay unconscious on the floor, in your head, as if you were reliving it, you could hear one of your dear mommy's memorable sayings: "What kind of idiot would put his hand into a device while its plugged in?! Only you, son. Only you!"
Soon you came to your sense and, while you still felt weak all over, you closed the rear panel and put the stereovision back in its place. At least you didn't ruin it.

You were so deeply engrossed in fulfilling your secret mission that you didn't notice that you exceeded the time allotted for the mission. That's why you were taken completely by surprise when the apartment's owner appeared accompanied by two hefty police officers, who, after threatening you with violence, forced you to lay on the floor with your hands in the air.
